key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve crystal morphology and suppress lattice defects, slowing ambient light- and heat-induced degradation compared with BA spacers in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ perovskite nanoflakes.
Evaluated light and thermal stability under ambient conditions.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative lifetime or solar-cell efficiency results, so improved material stability does not establish device-level durability or performance.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
